steps.description: Writing the prime factorisation of 20 and 30 in exponential form
steps.working:
Prime factorisation of 20 = 2 × 2 × 5 = 2² × 5
Prime factorisation of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5 = 2¹ × 3¹ × 5¹

steps.description: Calculating HCF from the prime factors
steps.working:
HCF(20, 30) = Product of the smallest power of each common prime factor
= 2¹ × 5¹ = 10

steps.description: Calculating LCM from the prime factors and stating final answers
steps.working:
LCM(20, 30) = Product of the greatest power of each prime factor involved
= 2² × 3¹ × 5¹ = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60
∴ HCF(20, 30) = 10 and LCM(20, 30) = 60

commonMistakes: Using the common division method (ladder method) instead of prime factorisation; CBSE awards zero or partial marks if the specified method is not used.
Confusing powers: selecting the highest power for HCF and lowest power for LCM.
Omitting the non-common factor (3) while calculating LCM.
7caca9b699e6b702ba982b6deb4b40ffddab7f74.examTip: Always express the prime factorisations in index/exponential form (e.g., 2² × 5) before writing HCF and LCM. This prevents power confusion and guarantees full step-marks under the CBSE marking scheme.
